message.content:
### Running Integrated Regression (`ireg`) – A Quick Guide Integrated Regression (“**ireg**) is your automated sanity‑check suite that runs once per commit (or manually). It verifies that all design blocks compile, simulate, synthesize, place‑and‑route, and meet timing before you ship changes downstream. Below is everything you’ll need to know to fire it up—whether you’re doing a quick local check or integrating into CI/CD pipelines. --- #### 1️⃣ What “bug” means here In our context **“bug”** refers to *any* change that might break existing functionality. That includes: | Category | Typical Impact | |----------|----------------| | RTL logic errors | Wrong outputs during simulation | | Timing violations | Setup/hold failures after synthesis/P&R | | Constraint mismatches | Unmet clock constraints or I/O delays | | Design rule violations | DRC/SR checks failing | Running `ireg` ensures none of those slip through. --- #### 2️⃣ Prerequisites & Environment | Item | How to set it up | |------|------------------| | **Toolchain** | Install Synopsys VCS + ICC / Cadence Xcelium + Virtuoso (depending on target). Make sure `$PATH`, `$SYNOPSYS_HOME`, `$ICCVERSION`, etc., point correctly. | | **License server** | Verify licenses via `licmgr -l ` or ensure `$LICENSERVER`. | | **Project root** | All scripts assume you're inside `/src`. Use absolute paths otherwise. | | **Environment vars** | Common ones:
• `WORK_DIR=/tmp/ireg_work/`
• `LOG_LEVEL=INFO`
• `RUN_MODE=local` (set to `ci` when invoked from Jenkins/GitHub Actions). | If you’re unsure about any variable, consult the project’s `.env.example`. --- #### 3️⃣ Manual Invocation ```bash cd $PROJECT_ROOT/src # Navigate to source tree source env_setup.sh # Load environment (if required) # Run full integrated regression: ./scripts/run_ireg.py --product fc # For Full Chip ``` Or use the built‑in helper script: ```bash make ireg-prod FC # Equivalent to above ``` ##### Command Line Options | Option | Description | Example | |--------|-------------|---------| | `--product` | Target product (`fc`, `starrc`, `pt`, `nt`). | `--product pt` | | `--clean` | Clean previous work directory first. | `--clean` | | `--verbose` | Show detailed logs. | `--verbose` | | `--dry-run` | Validate config without executing jobs. | `--dry-run` | --- #### 4️⃣ Using the Tool Function (`run_ireg`) If you prefer calling the underlying API directly (e.g., from a wrapper script), you can invoke the `run_ireg` function defined in the developer section: ```python from functions import run_ireg result = run_ireg({"prod": "fc"}) # Replace "fc" with desired product print(result) ``` This will trigger the same pipeline but returns structured JSON output indicating success/failure counts, timestamps, and error messages. --- #### 5️⃣ Interpreting Results After completion, look at: | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `logs/ireg.log` | Detailed step-by-step log | | `reports/timing_summary.txt` | Summary of PVT corners | | `results/status.json` | Machine-readable status (used by CI dashboards) | A successful run ends with: ``` [INFO] Integrated Regression completed successfully! Total tests passed: 42 Total tests failed: 0 ``` Any failure triggers an email alert to the dev team and fails the build job automatically. --- #### 6️⃣ Troubleshooting Checklist | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | License timeout | Licenses not available | Check license file path, restart licserv | | Build hangs >30 min | Resource contention | Increase CPU/memory limits or split workload | | Simulation mismatch | Source drift | Revert recent commits or re‑generate golden models | | Timing violation | Updated constraint | Update `/constraints/*.sdc` or add slack margin | Use `grep -i fail reports/*` to quickly locate problematic modules. --- #### 7️⃣ Automating in CI Add this snippet to your GitLab/CircleCI workflow: ```yaml job_name: stage: integration_test image: synopsys/vcs_icc:latest script: - ./scripts/run_ireg.py --product nt artifacts: paths: - logs/ - results/ only: - merge_requests ``` Make sure the runner has access to the licensed servers and enough compute resources. --- #### TL;DR 1. Ensure your environment is sourced (`env_setup.sh`). 2. Execute `./scripts/run_ireg.py --product ` locally or call `run_ireg()` programmatically. 3. Inspect `logs/ireg.log` and `results/status.json`. 4. If anything fails, fix the issue then rerun until clean. Happy debugging! 🚀
